name: brief-and-formula-intake
description: Normalizes a dev brief and a formula/spec into a single structured labeling intake record, so drafting and review prompts downstream have one consistent source instead of a scattered brief and spreadsheet.
when_to_use: A new SKU, reformulation, or line extension has a dev brief and a formula but no structured intake record yet.
what_to_use_for: Turning free-form brief text and a formula/spec sheet into a normalized record: SKU identity, formula table with quantities, intended serving size, claims mentioned in the brief, and a list of open questions or missing data blocking downstream drafting.
required_inputs: Dev brief (text or pasted document content); formula or spec sheet (ingredient list with quantities, sub-ingredient breakdowns if any); SKU identifier.
expected_outputs: Structured intake record (SKU identity, formula table, serving size, claims mentioned); open questions list; missing-data list, each item naming what is missing and what it blocks.
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: normalize a dev brief and a formula/spec into one structured labeling intake record for a beverage SKU.

Method:
1. Read the dev brief and the formula/spec I provide below.
2. Extract SKU identity (name, SKU code if given, package size, intended channel).
3. Build a formula table: each ingredient, its sub-ingredients if compound, and quantity or percentage as stated. Preserve the order given; do not reorder into predominance order, that is a separate downstream task.
4. Extract the intended serving size, if stated, and flag if it is absent.
5. List every claim mentioned anywhere in the brief (marketing copy, positioning language, or explicit claim language), verbatim.
6. Produce an open-questions list: anything ambiguous in the brief or formula that a human needs to resolve before drafting can start.
7. Produce a missing-data list: anything downstream drafting or review will need that is not present (for example: no serving size given, no allergen statement from the facility, no substantiation file referenced for a claim). For each item, name what it blocks.

Source of truth: the dev brief and formula/spec I provide are the only sources; do not infer facts not stated in them.

This is not a compliance judgment. Do not approve or reject any claim here; that is out of scope for this prompt. Surface ambiguity in the open-questions list rather than resolving it yourself.

Do not fabricate any figure, ingredient, or claim not present in the source materials. If something is unclear, put it in the open-questions list rather than guessing.

Return the complete file content, beginning with the YAML frontmatter block, ready to save at the path I specify, with no commentary outside the file content.

[Paste dev brief here]

[Paste formula/spec here]

SKU identifier: [SKU]

name: claims-target-scoping
description: Captures the claims a brief intends to make and classifies each by the FDA regulatory pathway it would need to clear, so downstream claims-compliance review starts from a scoped inventory instead of raw marketing copy.
when_to_use: After brief-and-formula-intake has produced an intake record, or whenever proposed claims and positioning copy exist for a SKU and need to be triaged before drafting or review.
what_to_use_for: Reading proposed claims and positioning copy, then tagging each distinct claim by claim type (nutrient content, structure/function, authorized health claim, or none of the above/marketing puffery) and the substantiation each pathway requires.
required_inputs: Proposed claims (list or extracted from brief/positioning copy); positioning copy (marketing language as drafted).
expected_outputs: Claim inventory: each claim, its claim-type tag, the regulatory pathway it falls under, and the substantiation required for that pathway; flags for any claim that does not cleanly fit a recognized pathway.
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: build a claim inventory from proposed claims and positioning copy, classifying each claim by its regulatory pathway.

Method:
1. Read every proposed claim and the positioning copy I provide below.
2. Extract each distinct claim as its own inventory row, verbatim as written.
3. For each claim, classify it into exactly one of: nutrient content claim (21 CFR 101.13 and Subpart D), implied nutrient content claim including "healthy" (21 CFR 101.65), structure/function claim, authorized health claim (21 CFR 101.14 and Subpart E), or non-regulated marketing language (no claim-type pathway).
4. For each classified claim, state the substantiation or disclosure that pathway requires (for example: a nutrient content claim needs the NFP value that supports it; a structure/function claim needs substantiation on file plus the required disclaimer; a health claim needs to match an FDA-authorized model claim).
5. Flag any claim that is ambiguous between two pathways, or that reads like an unauthorized disease claim, for human review rather than resolving the ambiguity yourself.
6. Do not judge whether any claim will pass; that is the job of the downstream claims-compliance prompts (nutrient-content-claim-review, structure-function-claim-review, prohibited-and-misleading-claim-screen, healthy-claim-eligibility-check). This prompt only scopes and tags.

Source of truth: the proposed claims and positioning copy I provide are the only sources.

Cite the exact CFR provision or statute for each pathway tag (21 CFR 101.13/Subpart D, 101.65, 101.14/Subpart E). If you cannot confirm the current text or status of a cited provision, say so explicitly rather than asserting it.

This is a scoping pass, not an approval. Do not mark any claim as compliant or cleared here.

Do not fabricate a claim, a pathway, or a substantiation requirement not grounded in the source text or in FDA's actual claim framework. Flag anything you cannot confirm.

Return the complete file content, beginning with the YAML frontmatter block, ready to save at the path I specify, with no commentary outside the file content.

[Paste proposed claims here]

[Paste positioning copy here]

SKU identifier: [SKU]
